title: Scientific notation
competency: Write very large and very small numbers in scientific notation and change them back to ordinary decimals.

keywords.def: Writing a number as a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10 and n an integer. Also called standard notation.

en.text: Scientific notation writes a number as a × 10ⁿ. The first part, a, is at least 1 and less than 10. Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit is in front. Count the moves. Moving left gives a positive n. Moving right gives a negative n.

am.text: ሳይንሳዊ አጻጻፍ ቁጥርን a × 10ⁿ አድርጎ ይጽፋል። a ቢያንስ 1 ሲሆን ከ10 ያንሳል። ከፊቱ አንድ ዜሮ ያልሆነ አሃዝ እስኪቀር የአስርዮሽ ነጥቡን አንቀሳቅስ። እንቅስቃሴዎቹን ቁጠር። ወደ ግራ ከሆነ n አዎንታዊ ነው። ወደ ቀኝ ከሆነ n አሉታዊ ነው።

screens.title: The long Abay
screens.text: The Abay (Blue Nile) river flows about 1,450,000 m through Ethiopia and Sudan.
screens.ask: Which of these equals 1,450,000? Take a guess.
screens.after:
All of them are equal: 1.45 × 1,000,000 = 14.5 × 100,000 = 145 × 10,000 = 1,450,000.
Many forms are possible, so we agree on one standard form. Read on.

screens.title: Slide the point
screens.text: Start with 1,450,000. Move the point left one place at a time.
steps: = 145 × 10⁴. Still more than one digit in front.
= 1.45 × 10⁶. Now one non-zero digit is in front. Stop.
The point moved 6 places left, so the power is 6.

screens.title: Scientific notation (standard notation)
paras: Science uses very large and very small numbers. For example:
The Abay (Blue Nile) river flows about 1,450,000 m through Ethiopia and Sudan.
The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is about 384,400 km.
A hydrogen atom has a mass of about 0.00000000000000000000000000167 kg.
screens.note: The printed book gives the Earth–Moon distance as 382,500 km. The usual value is about 384,400 km.

screens.title: Activity 1.24
paras: Many answers are possible, for example 48.600017 × 10.
That is why we agree on one standard form.

screens.title: Definition 1.15
defs: A number written as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer. Also called standard notation.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: Scientific notation: which number is written in scientific notation?
screens.why:
Scientific notation is a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10.
12.5 is 10 or more, and 0.8 is less than 1.
7 × 100 has the right value, but it must be written 7 × 10².
3.06 is between 1 and 10, and 10⁻² is a power of 10. So 3.06 × 10⁻² fits.
screens.clue: Check that the first factor is at least 1 and less than 10.

screens.title: Writing a number in standard form
steps: Move the decimal point until exactly one non-zero digit is in front of it.
Count the places moved. For a large number the point moves left and n is positive.
For a small number it moves right and n is negative.
(a) 1,856,700,000: the point moves 9 places left, so 1.8567 × 10⁹.
(b) 0.000000314: the point moves 7 places right, so 3.14 × 10⁻⁷.

screens.title: Changing back to decimals
paras: Example 2. Move the point back the other way.
screens.note: In Example 1(a), step 3 of the printed solution says "the decimal points will move to the right". For 1,856,700,000 it moves to the left.

screens.title: Standard form or not?
screens.text: Scientific notation: sort each number. Is the first factor at least 1 and less than 10?
screens.why:
The rule is a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10.
3.06, 7 and 1 pass the test.
12.5 and 45 are too big; 0.8 is too small.
The power can be positive or negative.
screens.clue: Look only at the number in front of × 10.

screens.title: Earth to Moon
screens.text: The Earth–Moon distance is about 384,400 km.
screens.why:
Move the point to sit after the first digit, 3: 3.84400.
Count the places it moved left: 5.
For a large number the power is positive.
So 384,400 = 3.844 × 10⁵.
screens.clue: Count how many places the point moves to sit after the 3.

screens.title: A small number
screens.text: Scientific notation for a small number: which is 0.00052?
screens.why:
Move the point right until it sits after the 5: 5.2.
It moved 4 places right, so the power is −4.
5.2 is between 1 and 10.
So 0.00052 = 5.2 × 10⁻⁴. 52 × 10⁻⁵ has the right value, but 52 is too big.
screens.clue: A small number has a negative power. Is the first factor between 1 and 10?

screens.title: A hydrogen atom
screens.text: A hydrogen atom has a mass of about 0.00000000000000000000000000167 kg.
screens.ask: Scientific notation: in standard form this is 1.67 × 10^___ kg.
screens.why:
There are 26 zeros after the point.
The point must also pass the 1: 26 + 1 = 27 places.
It moves right, so the power is negative.
So the mass is 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
screens.clue: Count the zeros after the point, then one more step to pass the 1.
screens.worked: There are 26 zeros after the point. The point must also pass the 1. That is 27 places to the right. So the mass is 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.why:
A negative power means move the point left.
Move it 7 places left: 1.7 → 0.17 → … → 0.00000017.
Check: 6 zeros after the point, then 17.
True.
screens.clue: A negative power means move the point left. Count 7 places.

items.why:
Move the point to sit after the 4: 4.8600017.
It moved 2 places left.
So the power is 2: 4.8600017 × 10².
items.clue: Count the places the point moves.

items.why:
Count the digits after the first 1: 4,580,000,000,000 has 13 digits.
So the point moves 13 places left.
14,580,000,000,000 = 1.458 × 10¹³.
items.clue: Count the digits after the first 1.

items.why:
Move the point right until it sits after the 6: 6.504.
It moved 4 places right, so the power is −4.
So 0.0006504 = 6.504 × 10⁻⁴.
10⁻³ counts only the zeros: the point must also pass the 6.
items.clue: Move the point to sit after the 6. Which way did it go?

items.why:
There are 12 zeros after the point.
One more place passes the 7: 13 places right.
So the power is −13.
0.00000000000078436 = 7.8436 × 10⁻¹³.
items.clue: Count the zeros after the point, then one more.

items.why:
Move the point to sit after the 1: 1.58762.
It moved 2 places left, so the power is 2.
So 158.762 = 1.58762 × 10².
15.8762 × 10 has the right value, but 15.8762 is too big.
items.clue: Only one non-zero digit may stand in front of the point.

items.why:
Move the point right to sit after the 8: 8.9.
It moved 5 places right.
Right means a negative power: −5.
So 0.000089 = 8.9 × 10⁻⁵.
items.clue: A small number has a negative power. Count the places.

items.why:
A positive power: move the point right.
Move it 6 places, filling with zeros: 1,340,000.
So 1.34 × 10⁶ = 1,340,000.
items.clue: A positive power means move the point right.

items.why:
A negative power: move the point left.
Move it 3 places: 3.3 → 0.33 → 0.033 → 0.0033.
So 3.3 × 10⁻³ = 0.0033.
items.clue: A negative power means move the point left.

items.why:
Both have the same power, 10³.
Add the first factors: 4.2 + 1.6 = 5.8.
So the sum is 5.8 × 10³.
10⁶ is wrong: adding numbers does not add the powers.
items.clue: The powers are the same. What happens to the first factors?

items.why:
Divide the first factors: 5.0 ÷ 2 = 2.5.
Divide the powers by subtracting: 10⁵ ÷ 10⁻² = 10⁵⁻⁽⁻²⁾.
5 − (−2) = 7, so 10⁷.
Answer: 2.5 × 10⁷.
items.clue: Divide the first factors. Subtract the powers.

test.why:
Move the point to sit after the 5: 5.672.
Count the places moved left: 8 (the digits after 5 are 67200000).
So 567,200,000 = 5.672 × 10⁸.

test.ask: Change back: 5.37 × 10⁶ as an ordinary number is ___
test.why:
A positive power: move the point right.
Move it 6 places: 5.37 → 5,370,000.
So 5.37 × 10⁶ = 5,370,000.

test.text: True or false? 0.8 × 10⁴ is in scientific notation.
test.why:
Scientific notation needs 1 ≤ a < 10.
0.8 is less than 1.
In standard form: 0.8 × 10⁴ = 8,000 = 8 × 10³.
So the statement is false.
